title: How to Find Hidden Apps on an Android Phone
html:
Hidden apps are usually hidden in one of four places. Check the full app list in Settings, the hide-apps list (on Samsung), Secure Folder (on Samsung), and private space (on Android 15 and newer). If you are checking your own phone, that covers the built-in ways. Only look through a phone you own or have the owner's permission to check.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Menu names vary by brand; use the Settings search box if you cannot find one.

I walked through these screens on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14, security update January 2025) on 10 Oct 2026.

1. The full list of apps in Settings

Open Settings, then Apps, then See all apps. Anything installed is listed here, even if it has no icon on your home screen. You can also swipe up from the bottom of the home screen and tap All apps. Google notes that some pre-installed system apps cannot be deleted, but on some phones you can turn them off so that they do not show on your list, and you can turn them back on.

If a name looks vague or you do not recognise it, tap it and read the App info page: which permissions it has, how much storage it uses and where it came from.

2. Samsung: the hide-apps list

On a Samsung Galaxy, apps can be hidden from the Home and Apps screens. Open Settings, then Home screen, then "Hide apps on Home and Apps screen". The list shows what is hidden. To show an app again, untick it.

On my vivo V23 Pro (Funtouch OS 14) the setting is called App hiding. It is listed on the Privacy screen under "Looking for other settings?", and Settings search finds it too. The screen says: "When hidden, the app will not show up on the home screen, the Recent apps interface, or some app lists, and you will not receive new messages from this app." Below that is a View hidden apps switch ("Swipe up with two fingers on the home screen to view hidden apps"), a Verify privacy password switch, and a list of every installed app with its own switch. On my phone the counter read "Hidden 0 apps". Because this phone can hide apps and silence their messages, the full list at Settings, then Apps, then All apps (136 apps installed on mine) is a better place to check than the home screen. I did not hide an app to test the hidden view.

3. Samsung: Secure Folder

Secure Folder is a separate, locked area for apps, files, pictures and videos. Open it from the Apps screen, or from Settings, then Security and privacy, then More security settings, then Secure Folder. The icon on the Apps screen can be switched off with "Add Secure Folder to Apps screen", so if you cannot see the icon, check that setting. You can also toggle it from the Quick Settings panel.

4. Android 15 and newer: private space

Private space is a locked area for apps. When it is locked, its apps are stopped, and Google says they are hidden from the launcher, recent apps, sharing screens and Settings, and cannot be found by search. To open it, scroll to the bottom of All apps and tap "Private space", or go to Settings, then Security and privacy, then Private, then Private space. It needs the device screen lock to open. It requires Android 15 or newer.

Deleting a private space deletes its apps and data, and the data cannot be restored from a backup, so do not delete one unless you are sure.

Apps that look normal but are not what they say

An app can have a harmless name and icon. Two settings help here: check Install unknown apps (Settings, then Apps, then Special app access) for anything that can install other apps, and run a Play Protect scan. Our guide to checking whether your phone is compromised goes through both. For permissions, see which apps can use your camera, mic and location.

What to do next

  1. Open Settings, Apps, See all apps, and read the list once.
  2. On Samsung, check the hide-apps list and Secure Folder.
  3. On Android 15 or newer, check private space.
  4. Remove or turn off what you do not recognise.
